children: According to CNBC, retirees who miss the Dec. 31 deadline for required minimum distributions (RMDs) may owe an IRS excise tax of up to 25% of the amount they should have withdrawn. Most retirees must begin taking RMDs from pretax accounts at age 73; the first withdrawal is due by April 1 of the following year, while later annual withdrawals are due by Dec. 31. Investors who correct a missed RMD within two years and file Form 5329 may reduce the penalty to 10%. A Vanguard analysis found that 7% of its investors at RMD age missed their annual withdrawal in 2025, compared with 6.7% in 2024.

title: Retirees Face Dec. 31 RMD Deadline, With Penalties Up to 25%
